title: Love from the heart
hook: they are true who love the Lord from the heart; those with one thing in the heart and another on the lips are false (Asa, Farid, ang 488)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Farid: rise, wash and bow, and admit the way is hard. Your line was the sufi of punjab.

A card goes around the office for someone's birthday. A page of signatures, nearly all saying the same thing: have a great one. One is from the person who complained about her all week, in handwriting just as cheerful as the rest. Nobody can tell from the card. That gap, between what's written outside and what's going on inside, is exactly where Farid puts his finger in one of his hymns.
screen: `A CARD FULL OF SIGNATURES.` → `THE SAME CHEERFUL HANDWRITING.` → `WHAT'S INSIDE?`

segments.voice: Farid's hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib aren't only short saloks. A few are longer shabads set to raag, sung like the Gurus' own. This one is in Raag Asa, on Ang 488, and it opens with a line simple to say and hard to live. In paraphrase: those who love the Lord from the heart are the true ones. Those who have one thing in the heart and another on the lips are counted false. Notice his words: dil, the heart, and muhabbat, love, the Sufi's language of love for the Beloved. Then he paints two kinds of people side by side. In paraphrase again: those dyed in the love of the Lord are delighted by the sight of Him. Those who forget the Name are a burden on the earth. Dyed is the picture. Dyed cloth doesn't have color painted on top; the color goes all the way through the thread. So the true one isn't the one with the loudest prayer. It's the one whose love goes all the way through, inside and outside the same color. And Farid isn't pointing at hypocrites in the street. The hymn holds a mirror. It's easy to say a warm thing with a cool heart, or to sign the card. The line doesn't ask for more words. It asks the words and the heart to match. For Sikhs this joins the Gurus' own teaching, that what is on the tongue should be what is in the mind. A Sufi's line, at home in the Sikh scripture.
screen: `A SHABAD IN RAAG ASA, ANG 488.` · `ONE THING IN THE HEART, ANOTHER ON THE LIPS.` · `DYED ALL THE WAY THROUGH.` · `NOT MORE WORDS: MATCHING WORDS.` · then, large: `THE HEART AND THE LIPS.`

segments.voice: Think back over the last day for one thing you said that didn't match what was inside: a yes you didn't mean, a fine that wasn't fine, a compliment with a cool heart behind it. Don't punish yourself; just look at the gap, and find the true sentence underneath it, said kindly. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.
Dil. Farid's word for the heart: those who love the Lord from the dil are the true ones, their lips saying the same thing.
Your line: the heart and the lips. Dyed in love, the color goes all the way through. Until tomorrow.
